question: The Indian government generally spends about % of GDP on healthcare
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (4): 1.2 is correct because public expenditure on healthcare in India has historically hovered around 1.2% to 1.3% of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP), one of the lowest proportions among developing and emerging economies before recent policy targets aimed to raise it to 2.5%. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): 12.2 - 12.2% of GDP is typical of high-income OECD nations with extensive socialized or privatized healthcare systems (such as the US or Germany), not India. • Option (2): 8.2 - 8.2% far exceeds India's government healthcare expenditure. • Option (3): 4.2 - 4.2% is higher than India's public health budget, although total healthcare spending including out-of-pocket private expenses reaches roughly 3–4%.

question: The women scientist who won Nobel prize in 2015 for her discovery on a novel therapy against malaria is
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (1): Youyou Tu is correct because Tu Youyou was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 2015 for her discovery of artemisinin (qinghaosu) from the sweet wormwood plant (Artemisia annua), which revolutionized malaria treatment and saved millions of lives globally. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (2): Svetlana Alexievich - Svetlana Alexievich won the 2015 Nobel Prize in Literature for her polyphonic writings on Soviet and post-Soviet life. • Option (3): Malala Yousafzai - Malala Yousafzai co-won the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize for her advocacy of girls' right to education. • Option (4): Alice Munro - Alice Munro won the 2013 Nobel Prize in Literature as a master of the contemporary short story.

question: International day for preservation of the Ozone layer is:
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (1): 16 September is correct because World Ozone Day is celebrated annually on 16 September to commemorate the signing of the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer in 1987, one of the most successful international environmental treaties. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (2): 2 October - 2 October is celebrated as Gandhi Jayanti (International Day of Non-Violence). • Option (3): 31 October - 31 October is observed in India as National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas) and World Cities Day. • Option (4): 27 November - 27 November is not associated with ozone layer preservation.

question: The Kalka Shimla railway is an example of
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (3): Narrow gauge railway is correct because the historic Kalka–Shimla Railway, built in 1898–1903 to connect Shimla (the summer capital of British India), operates on a 2 ft 6 in (762 mm) narrow gauge track and is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Mountain Railway of India. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): Broad gauge railway - Broad gauge uses a track width of 5 ft 6 in (1,676 mm), which forms the backbone of the standard Indian Railways network. • Option (2): Meter gauge railway - Meter gauge has a track width of exactly 1,000 mm (1 meter), different from the 762 mm narrow gauge of Kalka-Shimla. • Option (4): Monorail - A monorail runs on a single rail or beam, distinct from dual-rail narrow gauge mountain tracks.

question: Heavy floods in Kerala this year led to the outbreak of which of the following diseases?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (1): Leptospirosis is correct because following catastrophic floods in Kerala in 2018, stagnant floodwaters contaminated with the urine of infected rodents and livestock caused a major outbreak of Leptospirosis (locally known as rat fever), an acute zoonotic bacterial infection caused by Leptospira. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (2): Typhoid - While waterborne, typhoid did not form the primary outbreak epidemic reported during the post-flood crisis. • Option (3): Yellow fever - Yellow fever is an endemic tropical mosquito-borne flavivirus confined to parts of Africa and South America; it is not endemic in India. • Option (4): Influenza - Influenza is primarily a respiratory illness spread by airborne droplets, not flood-driven waterborne transmission.

question: Where was India's first specialized hospital for elephants unveiled on 17th November 2018?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (3): Mathura, Uttar Pradesh is correct because India's first specialized elephant hospital was opened on November 17, 2018, in Farah town of Mathura district, Uttar Pradesh, established by the wildlife conservation charity Wildlife SOS in collaboration with the UP Forest Department. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu - Coimbatore is home to elephant rehabilitation centers and sanctuaries in the Western Ghats, but not India's first specialized hospital. • Option (2): Wyanad, Kerala - Wayanad is a major wild elephant habitat in the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, but was not the location of this hospital. • Option (4): Coorg, Karnataka - Coorg houses Dubare Elephant Camp, but not the specialized elephant hospital unveiled in 2018.

question: Who performed the world's first heart transplant?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (3): Christian Bernard is correct because Dr. Christiaan Barnard, a South African cardiac surgeon, performed the world's first human-to-human heart transplant on 3 December 1967 at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town, South Africa, transplanting a heart into patient Louis Washkansky. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): Dr. Venugopal - Dr. P. Venugopal performed India's first successful heart transplant in 1994 at AIIMS, New Delhi. • Option (2): William Harvey - William Harvey discovered the systemic circulation of blood pumped by the heart in 1628. • Option (4): Robert Koch - Robert Koch was a pioneering German bacteriologist who identified the causative agents of tuberculosis, cholera, and anthrax.

question: Recently in Kerala, which highly infectious virus caused an outbreak?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (2): Nipah virus is correct because Kerala experienced severe localized outbreaks of Nipah virus (a zoonotic Henipavirus transmitted by fruit bats of the genus Pteropus) in Kozhikode and Malappuram districts starting in May 2018, characterized by acute encephalitis and high case fatality rates. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): Japanese encephalitis virus - Japanese encephalitis is a flavivirus transmitted by Culex mosquitoes prevalent in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Assam. • Option (3): Ebola virus - Ebola virus causes severe hemorrhagic fever in Central and West Africa; no outbreak has occurred in India. • Option (4): Zika virus - Zika virus outbreaks in India occurred later in Gujarat, Rajasthan, and isolated cases in Kerala, but the prominent deadly outbreak in 2018 was caused by Nipah.

question: How many megabytes (MB) are there in one gigabyte (GB):
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (4): 1024 is correct because in computer binary architecture, storage prefixes follow powers of 2. One gigabyte (GB) equals 2^10 = 1024 megabytes (MB). ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): 1000 - 1000 MB is based on decimal (SI base-10) prefixes, but computer architecture standardly defines 1 GB as 1024 MB. • Option (2): 2000 - 2000 is double the decimal gigabyte. • Option (3): 220 - 220 is unrelated to binary or decimal memory units.

question: RAM in computers usually stands for:
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (3): Random access memory is correct because RAM stands for Random Access Memory, the primary volatile memory of a computer that allows data to be read and written in roughly the same amount of time regardless of its physical location inside the memory chip. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): Remove All Memory - A fictitious phrase not related to computing terms. • Option (2): Read and memorize - An informal description, not the technical computing acronym. • Option (4): Roast all mice - A humorous distractor with no scientific relevance.

question: Our National science Day is celebrated on February 28 to honour which scientist's discovery?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (1): Sir C V Raman is correct because National Science Day is celebrated in India every year on February 28 to commemorate Sir C.V. Raman's discovery of the Raman Effect (inelastic scattering of photons) on 28 February 1928, for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (2): Homi J Bhaba - Dr. Homi Jehangir Bhabha was the father of the Indian nuclear program and founding director of TIFR and BARC. • Option (3): APJ Abdul Kalam - Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam was the Missile Man of India and 11th President; his birthday (October 15) is celebrated as World Students' Day. • Option (4): Jagdish Chander Bose - Sir J.C. Bose pioneered millimeter-wave radio transmission and plant physiology (crescograph).

question: Golden revolution refers to:
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (3): Production of horticulture is correct because the Golden Revolution in India (1991–2003, spearheaded by Nirpakh Tutej) refers to the period of very high growth in the production of horticulture (fruits, vegetables) and honey. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): Gold demonetization - Gold demonetization is an economic policy, not an agricultural revolution. • Option (2): Production of oil seeds - Production of oilseeds is known as the Yellow Revolution (led by Sam Pitroda). • Option (4): Production of eggs - Production of eggs and poultry is known as the Silver Revolution (initiated under Indira Gandhi).

question: One kilometre is equal to how many miles?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (4): 0.62 is correct because one kilometer equals approximately 0.621371 miles (or 1 mile ≈ 1.60934 kilometers). ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): 0.84 - 0.84 miles would equal about 1.35 kilometers. • Option (2): 0.5 - 0.5 miles is half a mile, equal to 0.805 km. • Option (3): 6 - 6 miles is almost 10 kilometers.

question: Which of the following is NOT a Kharif crop?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (2): Mustard is correct because Mustard (Brassica juncea) is a Rabi (winter-sown) crop sown in October–November and harvested in spring (March–April). Rice, maize, and sugarcane are typical Kharif crops sown with the onset of the monsoon in June–July. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): Maize - Maize is a staple Kharif crop requiring warm weather and monsoon rains. • Option (3): Rice - Rice (paddy) is the primary Kharif crop of India. • Option (4): Sugarcane - Sugarcane is planted in Kharif/autumn and requires extensive water and long maturation.

question: Which of the following is NOT a SAARC country?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (4): Indonesia is correct because the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) consists of 8 South Asian member nations: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. Indonesia is a Southeast Asian nation and a founding member of ASEAN, not SAARC. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): Afghanistan - Afghanistan became the 8th member state of SAARC in 2007. • Option (2): Pakistan - Pakistan is a founding member of SAARC (1985). • Option (3): Nepal - Nepal is a founding member and hosts the SAARC Secretariat in Kathmandu.

question: Headquarters of United Nations (UNO) are in:
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (2): New York is correct because the official headquarters of the United Nations is situated in the Turtle Bay neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, USA, on international territory established in 1952. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): Geneva - Geneva, Switzerland hosts the Palace of Nations and the UN European office, but not the global primary UN headquarters. • Option (3): Sydney - Sydney, Australia does not host the headquarters of the United Nations. • Option (4): Washington - Washington, D.C. hosts the headquarters of the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF), but not the UN.

question: WHO declared COVID-19 as a Pandemic on:
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (4): 11th March, 2020 is correct because World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus officially characterized COVID-19 as a global pandemic during a media briefing on 11 March 2020, following alarming levels of spread and severity across 114 countries. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): 1st January, 2020 - On 1 January 2020, WHO set up its Incident Management Support Team across the three organizational levels. • Option (2): 1st December, 2019 - December 2019 marks when the earliest retrospective cases of atypical pneumonia were documented in Wuhan, China. • Option (3): 30th January, 2020 - On 30 January 2020, WHO declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC), which preceded the formal pandemic declaration.

question: Maximum ozone layer is found in which layer of Atmosphere?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (2): Stratosphere is correct because approximately 90% of the Earth's atmospheric ozone resides in the stratosphere (predominantly between 15 km and 35 km altitude), where it forms the ozone layer that absorbs biologically hazardous solar ultraviolet (UV-B and UV-C) radiation. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): Troposphere - The troposphere contains only about 10% of atmospheric ozone, where it acts as a pollutant and greenhouse gas (photochemical smog). • Option (3): Mesosphere - The mesosphere (50–85 km) has extremely thin air and negligible ozone concentration. • Option (4): Thermosphere - The thermosphere (85–600 km) is dominated by ionized gases and solar X-ray absorption, lacking an ozone layer.

question: The theme of World Immunization Week 2021 is:
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (1): Vaccines bring us closer is correct because the World Health Organization designated 'Vaccines bring us closer' as the global theme for World Immunization Week 2021 (celebrated in the last week of April), urging greater global engagement around immunization to connect people to a healthier future. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (2): Vaccinate daughter, screen mothers - A slogan frequently used in cervical cancer HPV vaccination campaigns, not the 2021 Immunization Week theme. • Option (3): Vaccines work for all - '#VaccinesWork for All' was the campaign theme for World Immunization Week 2020. • Option (4): Protect your world-get vaccinated - 'Protect your world - get vaccinated' was the theme used in World Immunization Week 2012.

question: One yard is equal to how many inches?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (1): 36 is correct because in the imperial and US customary systems of measurement, 1 yard equals exactly 3 feet, and each foot contains 12 inches; thus, 1 yard = 3 × 12 = 36 inches. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (2): 3 - 3 is the number of feet in a yard, not inches. • Option (3): 91.44 - 91.44 is the length of one yard in centimeters (1 yard = 91.44 cm). • Option (4): 12 - 12 is the number of inches in one foot.

question: Which of the following variant is known as the Delta variant of SARS-CoV-2?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (1): Lineage B.1.617.2 is correct because under the WHO Greek-alphabet nomenclature for SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern, the Delta variant corresponds to PANGO lineage B.1.617.2, first detected in India in late 2020. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (2): Lineage B.1.1.7 - Lineage B.1.1.7 is the Alpha variant, first identified in the United Kingdom. • Option (3): Lineage B.1.351 - Lineage B.1.351 is the Beta variant, first detected in South Africa. • Option (4): Lineage P.1 - Lineage P.1 is the Gamma variant, first identified in Brazil.

question: COVID-19 mRNA vaccines give instructions to body's cells to make the "spike protein." Which of the following is an m-RNA vaccine for COVID-19?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (1): Pfizer-BioTech vaccine is correct because the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine (BNT162b2 / Comirnaty) is an mRNA vaccine that utilizes lipid nanoparticle-formulated nucleoside-modified messenger RNA encoding the prefusion spike glycoprotein of SARS-CoV-2. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (2): Oxford-Astra Zeneca vaccine - The Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine (Covishield/ChAdOx1 nCoV-19) is a replication-deficient chimpanzee adenovirus vector vaccine, not an mRNA vaccine. • Option (3): Bharat Biotech vaccine - Bharat Biotech's Covaxin (BBV152) is an inactivated whole-virion vaccine formulated with an alum/imidazoquinoline adjuvant. • Option (4): Russia's Sputnik vaccine - Sputnik V (Gam-COVID-Vac) is a recombinant human adenoviral vector vaccine (Ad26 and Ad5).

question: Harvey J Alter, Charles M Rice and Michael Houghton won the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 2020 For:
options: for discoveries about how cells sense and adapt to oxygen availability
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (1): identification of Hepatitis C virus is correct because the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded jointly to Harvey J. Alter, Michael Houghton, and Charles M. Rice for their landmark discovery and characterization of the Hepatitis C virus (HCV). ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (2): work on black holes - Roger Penrose, Reinhard Genzel, and Andrea Ghez won the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics for their work on black hole formation and the supermassive compact object at the galactic center. • Option (3): developing the CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing tools - Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer A. Doudna won the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing. • Option (4): for discoveries about how cells sense and adapt to oxygen availability - William G. Kaelin Jr., Sir Peter J. Ratcliffe, and Gregg L. Semenza won the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for cellular oxygen-sensing discoveries (HIF pathway).

question: Which city is known as 'Gold capital of the World'?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (1): Johannesburg is correct because Johannesburg in South Africa is famously called 'Egoli' (the City of Gold or Gold Capital of the World) because it was founded following the discovery of immense gold deposits along the Witwatersrand gold reef in 1886, producing a significant fraction of the world's all-time mined gold. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (2): Paris - Paris is nicknamed the 'City of Light' (La Ville Lumière), famous for art, fashion, and culture. • Option (3): Dubai - Dubai is nicknamed the 'City of Gold' for its modern retail gold souks, but historically and geographically Johannesburg is recognized as the world's gold mining capital. • Option (4): London - London is a premier global financial hub and home to the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA), but not known as the Gold Capital of the World.

question: The World Health Organization (WHO) has certified which country as Malaria free in 2021?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (2): China is correct because on 30 June 2021, the World Health Organization officially awarded China a malaria-free certification, following 70 years of targeted public health efforts that reduced cases from 30 million annually in the 1940s to zero indigenous cases since 2017. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): Pakistan - Pakistan remains endemic for malaria with millions of clinical cases reported annually. • Option (3): Brazil - Brazil still has significant endemic transmission of Plasmodium vivax and falciparum in the Amazon basin. • Option (4): Canada - Canada was certified malaria-free decades ago and does not represent the newly certified country in 2021.

question: Which of the following is not an anti-virus Software?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (3): Oracle is correct because Oracle Corporation is a multinational enterprise software and technology company famous for its relational database management systems (RDBMS), enterprise resource planning (ERP), and cloud infrastructure, not antivirus protection software. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): Avira - Avira is a well-known German computer antivirus and cybersecurity software provider. • Option (2): Bitdefender - Bitdefender is a globally recognized Romanian cybersecurity and antivirus software company. • Option (4): Panda - Panda Security is a Spanish cybersecurity firm famous for developing cloud-based antivirus tools.

question: GPS is an abbreviation for?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (3): Global Positioning System is correct because GPS stands for Global Positioning System, a satellite-based radionavigation system owned by the United States government and operated by the United States Space Force that provides geolocation and time information to a GPS receiver anywhere on or near the Earth. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): Global Poles System - A meaningless phrase not related to navigational satellites. • Option (2): Global Positioning Store - A distractor incorporating commercial terminology. • Option (4): Global Positioning Satellite - While GPS employs satellites, the acronym refers to the entire satellite-and-ground 'System'.

question: According to Indian law, what is the minimum age of a person for employment in a factory?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (2): 14 years is correct because under Article 24 of the Constitution of India and Section 67 of the Factories Act 1948 (amended under the Child and Adolescent Labour Act), no child below the age of 14 years is permitted to be employed or permitted to work in any factory, mine, or other hazardous occupations. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): 12 years - Employing children at 12 years is strictly illegal under Indian child labor laws. • Option (3): 18 years - 18 years is the age of majority and minimum age for hazardous factory employment, but general non-hazardous factory legal employment threshold begins above 14 with adolescent protections. • Option (4): 21 years - 21 years is not the minimum legal age for factory labor.

question: Which of the following phases of clinical trial evaluates safety and tolerability of a drug in healthy Volunteers?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (1): Phase 1 is correct because Phase 1 clinical trials are initial human studies typically conducted on a small cohort (20–100) of healthy adult human volunteers to establish safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic profiles, and maximum tolerated dose (safe dosage range). ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (2): Phase IIA - Phase IIA trials are pilot clinical studies designed to assess initial therapeutic efficacy and dosing requirements in patient populations with the targeted disease. • Option (3): Phase III - Phase III trials are large-scale, randomized controlled comparative trials conducted on hundreds to thousands of patients to demonstrate statistical therapeutic efficacy versus standard of care or placebo. • Option (4): Phase 11B - Phase IIB (often miswritten as 11B) focuses on determining optimal dose-ranging and therapeutic efficacy in disease patients, not initial safety in healthy volunteers.

question: Ethyl mercaptan added to the otherwise odourless LPG cooking gas for imparting a detectable smell to the gas is a compound of:
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (3): Sulphur is correct because Ethyl mercaptan (ethanethiol, CH3CH2SH) is an organosulfur compound possessing a strong, repulsive garlic/rotten-egg odor that can be detected by humans at concentrations of less than one part per billion, serving as an effective stenching odorant in LPG to warn of dangerous leaks. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): Bromine - Bromine is a halogen used in flame retardants and water purification, not in LPG odorants. • Option (2): Oxygen - Ethanethiol contains sulfur, hydrogen, and carbon (CH3CH2SH); it does not contain oxygen (an alcohol would have -OH instead of -SH). • Option (4): Nitrogen - Nitrogen is not present in ethyl mercaptan.

question: "Operation Flood" is a movement related with the Product:
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (1): Milk is correct because Operation Flood, launched on 13 January 1970 by the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) and led by Dr. Verghese Kurien (the 'Father of the White Revolution'), was the world's largest agricultural development program, transforming India from a milk-deficient nation into the world's largest milk producer. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (2): Fresh Water - Operation Flood did not involve water management; water initiatives include the Jal Jeevan Mission and National Water Mission. • Option (3): Rice - Rice production was revolutionized under the Green Revolution, led by M.S. Swaminathan in India. • Option (4): Rain - Cloud seeding and monsoon missions deal with precipitation, not Operation Flood.

question: Indian Standard Time (IST) refers to the local time of which city?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (3): Mirzapur near Allahabad is correct because Indian Standard Time (IST) is calculated based on the 82.5° E longitude (82°30' E) meridian, which passes through Mirzapur (near Prayagraj/Allahabad in Uttar Pradesh), fixing IST at exactly UTC+05:30. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): Banaras - Varanasi (Banaras) lies nearby in UP but does not sit on the official standard time meridian (82.5° E). • Option (2): Gurugram near Delhi - Gurugram lies near 77° E longitude, about 5.5 degrees west of the standard time meridian. • Option (4): Kolkata - Kolkata lies near 88.3° E longitude, having previously observed Calcutta Time until 1948.

question: During an outbreak of a viral infection, all health care workers are advised to wear personal protective equipment. For the purpose, N95 respirators were also provided. What does N95 stands for?
options: Non-oil proof, blocks 95% of very small (0.3 micron) test particles
Non-oil proof, blocks 98% of very small (0.03 micron) test particles
Non-oil proof, blocks 95% of very small (0.003 micron) test particles
Non-oil proof, blocks 98% of very small (0.3 micron) test particles
correct_answer: Non-oil proof, blocks 95% of very small (0.3 micron) test particles
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (1): Non-oil proof, blocks 95% of very small (0.3 micron) test particles is correct because under NIOSH (US National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health) particulate respirator standards, 'N' stands for 'Not resistant to oil', and '95' means the filter blocks at least 95% of airborne test particles with a mass median aerodynamic diameter of 0.3 micrometers (the most penetrating particle size). ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (2): Non-oil proof, blocks 98% of very small (0.03 micron) test particles - The particle size rating is 0.3 microns, not 0.03 microns, and efficiency is 95%, not 98%. • Option (3): Non-oil proof, blocks 95% of very small (0.003 micron) test particles - 0.003 microns is far below the standardized 0.3 micron aerodynamic challenge particle size. • Option (4): Non-oil proof, blocks 98% of very small (0.3 micron) test particles - 98% filtration efficiency is not a standard NIOSH rating (95, 99, and 100 are the NIOSH ratings).

question: The material used as a bioplastic is:
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (3): Polyhydroxybutyrate is correct because Polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) is a naturally occurring polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) synthesized by bacteria (such as Cupriavidus necator or Bacillus megaterium) as an intracellular energy storage polymer; it is fully biodegradable, renewable, and extensively used as a bioplastic. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): Polystyrene - Polystyrene is a synthetic, petroleum-derived, non-biodegradable polymer (used in thermocol and foam). • Option (2): Polypropylene - Polypropylene is a conventional commodity thermoplastic made by polymerizing petroleum-derived propylene. • Option (4): Dextran - Dextran is a complex branched glucan used as an antithrombotic and plasma volume expander, not as structural bioplastic.

question: The script used in Sumerian Civilization is known as:
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (1): Cuneiform is correct because Cuneiform (meaning 'wedge-shaped', from Latin cuneus) was the writing system invented by the Sumerians in southern Mesopotamia around 3400–3200 BCE, inscribed on wet clay tablets using a blunt reed stylus. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (2): Hieroglyphics - Hieroglyphs were the formal writing system utilized in Ancient Egypt. • Option (3): Pictographic - While cuneiform evolved from early pictograms, the formal script of Sumer is universally recognized as Cuneiform. • Option (4): Phonetic - Phonetic script developed much later (e.g., Phoenician alphabet), whereas Sumerian was a logo-syllabic script.

question: Which city is known as 'iron capital of the World'?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (4): Pittsburgh is correct because Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA is globally renowned as the 'Iron City' or 'Steel City' (Iron Capital of the World) due to its historic dominance in the iron and steel manufacturing industries, driven by its confluence of rivers and abundant coal deposits. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): Johannesburg - Johannesburg is the Gold Capital of the World, not the iron capital. • Option (2): Paris - Paris is renowned for the Eiffel Tower (made of wrought iron), but is not known as the iron capital of the world. • Option (3): Dubai - Dubai is famous for architecture and finance, not iron or steel manufacturing dominance.

question: Aspirin was derived from the acetylsalicylic acid found in:
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (2): Willow tree bark is correct because Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) was synthesized by Felix Hoffmann at Bayer in 1897 as a safer derivative of salicylic acid, the active antipyretic and analgesic component originally extracted from the bark and leaves of the white willow tree (Salix alba). ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): Petri dish containing bacteria - Bacteria in petri dishes were involved in discovering many antibiotics (e.g., streptomycin from Streptomyces), not aspirin. • Option (3): Petri dish containing fungi - Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in a fungal culture of Penicillium notatum, not aspirin. • Option (4): Mushrooms - Mushrooms produce various psychoactive and toxic alkaloids (like psilocybin or amanitin), not acetylsalicylic acid.

question: Legal limit of blood alcohol concentration as per traffic rules in India is:
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (1): 30 mg in 100ml blood is correct because under Section 185 of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 of India, a driver is legally guilty of driving under the influence (DUI) if their blood alcohol concentration (BAC) exceeds 30 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood (0.03% BAC), as measured by a breath analyzer test. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (2): 60 mg in 100 ml blood - 60 mg per 100 ml is double the legal permissible limit in India. • Option (3): 50 mg in 100 ml blood - 50 mg per 100 ml (0.05%) is the legal limit in several European countries (like France and Germany), but India enforces 30 mg. • Option (4): 40 mg in 100 ml blood - 40 mg per 100 ml exceeds the 30 mg threshold prescribed by Indian law.

question:
